correctness.rationale: From the primary Eq. (3.7) reliability integral β1 e²∫1∞t^(β1−1)exp(−t^β1−t^β2)dt, the magnitude of its formal n-th upper-incomplete-gamma term is a_n=Γ(1+nr,1)/n!, r=β2/β1>0. For n→∞ the lower cutoff 1 is negligible relative to Γ(1+nr); Stirling gives log a_n=(r−1)n log n+n(r log r−r+1)+O(log n). If r>1 terms grow; at r=1, Γ(n+1,1)/n!→1; neither series can converge. If 0<r<1, ∫1∞β1e²t^(β1−1) exp(−t^β1+t^β2)dt is finite and exactly dominates absolute termwise exponential expansion, so Tonelli/Fubini and the gamma formula are valid. At equal shapes independent continuous equal laws give R=1/2; for opposite ordering R(β1,β2)=1−R(β2,β1), yielding the valid three-branch formula for all βi>0 at common α,λ. Direct bounded gamma asymptotic spot checks at r=1/2,1,3/2 with n=5,10,20 independently display decay, unit-size terms, and growth; analytic Stirling/dominated-interchange prove the full boundary. The source integral itself remains valid and finite.
